pr_title: Adjust osu! autoplay generation to ensure constant SPM with rate-changing mods
pr_body:
Closes #10283.

A few notes to explain things:

The first thing that this PR does to achieve its end result is allow autoplay implementations to access the list of mods used to generate the autoplay replay for. I've gone ahead and marked the old `CreateReplayScore()` method as obsolete in favour of the one that accepts mods - consumers can always ignore the mods. Curious if you agree with this choice, and I'll split this part of the PR (essentially the first commit) on request.

Secondly, most of the pieces in place to achieve this (the same way that stable seems to do) were in place already in `OsuAutoGeneratorBase`, in the way of two methods: `ApplyModsToRate(double)` and `ApplyModsToTime(double)`. Unfortunately, `ModTimeRamp` - which was not in stable - is a major complication to these methods, as the track rate in it depends on track time, which kills the simple calculations.

I've managed to somewhat salvage that structure by moving stuff around. All call sites of `ApplyModsToRate()` now need to accept a track time instant to be able to transform time correctly - in particular some things that were constants previously, now can't be for exactly that reason, and are usually replaced with private/protected methods that calculate these constants for a given time instant (see `FrameDelay` and `reactionTime`).

The worse part was `ApplyModsToTime()`. The transformation of track time to real time for `ModTimeRamp` is - I'm pretty sure - non-linear. [I thought I had the formula for it right](https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/10283#issuecomment-771241482), but it was just slightly off, and it was inscrutable anyway. Thankfully today I realised there is an alternative - because all usages of that method were usually called on time *deltas*, not actual time instants, then I can perform a local approximation for that delta by just dividing by the track rate at a given time instant. It's not perfectly correct, but seems to work well enough in practice.

I've both tested this manually [on this map](https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmapsets/679738) and added automated test cases. Note that scrubbing the replay will break this because it's presumably playing back past frames with a future rate, but that's a separate issue and this pull is too large as-is to meaningfully address that anyway.
pr_comments: I think I can get behind the general structure of these changes (definitely better than the alternatives we've tried previously), but can you elaborate on the seeking hypothesis you have? Is the "applying a future rate" something happening elsewhere as a completely separate issue? Just trying to imagine what is going on there so I can ignore the issue while reviewing this if feasible.

I'd have to take a proper second look to confirm what might be going on for sure, but my working surface level hypothesis was that `ModTimeRamp` instantaneously applies track rate after seeking, therefore desyncing the replay with the actual gameplay (frames in the past relative to the seek point now get the future rate multiplier valid at the seek point itself - see `RateAdjustedRotation`).

Aha, I think I can understand what's going on there, with the gameplay clock (playing catch-up) vs the audio clock (already seeked to the final position with the latter rate applied).

At some point we need to get the audio synced with current gameplay position, that was one of the end goals with seeking - to have the audio speed up during accelerated playback (and fade out if it gets too fast that bass can't handle it etc.). For another day, for sure.

issue_context.title: Autoplay spinning speed depends on rate-changing mods
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:** 
The bonus score of a spinner with DT mod is capped by the maximum attainable spinner bonus score (i.e. at 477 rpm / auto). Notice in the video when the map is played with DT, the first spinner does not go pass 850 for its bonus score even with auto mod, which is the spinner score auto mod got for that spinner when played with NM

**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:** 
https://streamable.com/m3l50j

**osu!lazer version:** 
2020.925.0

**Logs:**
[database.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/5295003/database.log)
[performance-audio.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/5295005/performance-audio.log)
[performance-draw.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/5295006/performance-draw.log)
[performance-update.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/5295007/performance-update.log)
[performance.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/5295008/performance.log)
[runtime.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/5295009/runtime.log)
comments: The actual issue is that autoplay is spinning too fast on DT and too slow on HT. Notice the SPM counter. Spinners should have the same SPM regardless of rate-changing mods.

I noticed that too, but anecdotally I think rate changing mods also give you extra/reduced max spinner bonus if DT/HT is used in stable, but in this case the bonus stopped increasing after a certain amount with DT, tho I'm not sure if I have confused something
That is not a duplicate as the previous one (#9821) has been resolved in release `2020.814.0`, while this one is reported in release `2020.925.0`.
Adding to milestone; we should probably come to a conclusion as to how this should be working.

As an update, I have 99% of this ready, except for one thing - `ModTimeRamp`. I cannot for the life of me figure out the correct time transformation to apply to the replay generation process in order to keep the spinning rate at a constant 477 with that one.

I thought something like this was going to be correct, but it's still off by a noticeable margin...

![2021-02-02-004649_1832x982_scrot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20418176/106532332-4e172380-64f0-11eb-9cf4-153c238987d5.png)

(`r_0` and `r_f` are starting and final track rates, correspondingly, `t_0` and `t_f` are ramp start and end times, `a` is acceleration. This is all derived from equations of constant acceleration motion.)

review_comments: I think this is going to change the runtime behaviour of the mod to be less smooth in the ramping, no? Not sure if it's enough to be audible (and whether it sounds bad) yet, but worth noting.
I think that was the case already. The bindable was rounding on its own anyways due to the precision set.
Oh. Well then. I plan on testing this out to see how it feels sounds, but should be fine in that case.
